status: Targeted primary-source reading and official-code inspection, not full protocol extraction or model evaluation.

inspected_sections: Main text: RNA strand translocation and ionic-current detection
Online Methods: screening translocases, adapter design, preparation of RNA for sequencing
primary_sources.access_limit: Publisher page offered subscription preview; full primary-paper PDF read at university mirror. No numeric recipe transcribed from OCR. Modern protocols were not substituted for this version.

facts.reported: This version describes ligating poly(A)+ RNA to a poly(T)-bearing adapter with T4 DNA ligase; a motor-loaded sequencing adapter is subsequently ligated.
The method physically reads RNA through a nanopore ionic-current signal; RNA-compatible motor and signal interpretation are part of the readout architecture.

derived_rules: Reagent names are insufficient substrate evidence.
Identify the molecule sensed and the decoder; do not impose RT, PCR or DNA barcodes on every sequencing technology.
An original protocol version and a later library-preparation variant are distinct evidence scopes.

inspected_sections: Target article main text workflow and Figure 1A; target begins after preceding article in compound PDF
primary_sources.access_limit: Original supplementary PDF exceeded web reader limit and was not read; no detailed reaction recipe is claimed here.

facts.reported: The reported sequence crosslinks chromatin, digests DNA, fills restriction ends with biotin labeling, ligates under dilution, then shears and enriches biotin-marked junctions for sequencing.

derived_rules: The information role of a ligation junction can be genomic-pair proximity rather than an amplification or instrument handle.
A narrowly declared DNA-end-joining family must not establish equivalence of the larger information-recording transformation.
